blloku: How much does an apartment cost in Blloku, Tirana?

New builds in Blloku run roughly 3,000 to 5,500 euros per square metre as of 2026, and resale sits at about 2,500 to 3,500. That is the highest residential band in Albania. Prices have climbed 22 to 37 percent since 2023, when off-plan units were being booked around 3,500.
Is Blloku a good investment in 2026?

Blloku is where you preserve capital, not where you maximise yield. It has the city's most expensive rents, strong short-let demand and the deepest resale liquidity in Albania. The catch is arithmetic: prices have risen faster than rents since 2023, so the gross yield ceiling here is lower than in cheaper districts.
What are the drawbacks of living in Blloku?

Noise, traffic and parking. Blloku is the centre of Tirana's bar, boutique and office life, which is exactly what makes it desirable and exactly what makes it loud. Roughly 27 percent of buyers in the central zone are non-residents, so a meaningful share of neighbours are absent owners or short-let guests.
liqeni-artificial: How much does property near Tirana's Artificial Lake cost?

The Artificial Lake is the most expensive reference zone in Tirana at 227,400 lek per square metre. Off-plan units run about 2,400 to 2,700 euros per square metre in 2026, and around 2,700 near the dam. A luxury tower here set the national record at 10,000 euros per square metre.
Why is the Artificial Lake area so expensive?

It holds the city's main green asset. The lake and Olympic Park give central Tirana its only large park, and apartments overlooking it are scarce, which is what carries the 227,400 lek per square metre reference price. Buyers are concentrated among Albanian high earners and foreign purchasers.
Is a lake view worth the premium?

Not automatically. The view premium here is not consistently supported by rental income: tenants pay for location, size and condition far more than for an outlook. Treat the premium as a lifestyle and capital-preservation purchase rather than a yield play, and compare the actual achieved rent in the building before paying it.
komuna-e-parisit: How much does an apartment cost in Komuna e Parisit?

Off-plan bookings start around 3,000 euros per square metre in 2026, with completed stock near 2,700. The White Tower project sold at about 2,700, roughly 17 percent above its 2023 off-plan price. That places Komuna e Parisit just below Blloku while offering considerably more quiet.
Is Komuna e Parisit good for families?

It is Tirana's family prime. The district sits beside the Grand Park, holds a cluster of embassies, and draws long-term expatriate and professional households rather than short-let traffic. That mix gives it steadier year-round rental demand than the nightlife districts, and a calmer street environment for children.
What is the main drawback of Komuna e Parisit?

Parking. The district was not built for current car ownership, and on-street space is the recurring complaint from residents. If a listing includes a dedicated parking place, that is a real part of its value here rather than an optional extra, and it is worth confirming in writing before you commit.
myslym-shyri: How much does an apartment cost on Myslym Shyri?

New builds run about 2,000 to 2,500 euros per square metre in 2026 and resale sits at roughly 1,500 to 2,000. Myslym Shyri is materially cheaper than Blloku while remaining walking distance from the centre, which is the trade most family buyers in Tirana are actually making.
Is Myslym Shyri a good area to buy in Tirana?

It is the most liquid mid-market district in the city. Demand comes from local families and long-term tenants rather than tourists, so occupancy holds through winter, and the resale pool is genuinely deep. For year-round rental income rather than seasonal upside, it is our first choice in Tirana.
What kind of tenant does Myslym Shyri attract?

Local families and working professionals on long leases. The street itself is a commercial spine with everyday retail, which supports steady demand rather than the seasonal peaks of the centre. Expect lower headline rents than Blloku and considerably fewer void months, which is usually the better trade on a two-bedroom.
qender-tirana: How much does an apartment cost in central Tirana?

Older stock in the centre runs about 1,500 to 2,500 euros per square metre in 2026, and new projects near Skanderbeg Square reach 3,000 to 3,500. Inside the small ring road new builds start around 2,300, and finding anything below 2,000 euros per square metre is now effectively impossible.
Is the centre of Tirana a good place to buy?

It offers the deepest liquidity and the widest quality spread in the country. The centre mixes 1,500 euro per square metre older stock with 3,500 euro new build on the same streets, so the district average tells you very little. Inspect the specific building rather than trusting the zone price.
What are the downsides of central Tirana?

Noise, tourist footfall and a highly uneven building stock. The same square kilometre holds carefully renovated apartments and pre-2000 blocks that carry a permanent structural discount after the 2019 earthquake. Age of construction matters more to your outcome here than the postcode does.
pazari-i-ri: Is Pazari i Ri good for short-term rentals?

On our assessment it has the strongest short-let potential in Tirana. The market was renovated in 2016 and became the city's main tourist and dining hub, which concentrates visitor demand into a small, walkable area. New projects near the square run about 3,000 to 3,500 euros per square metre.
How much does property cost around Pazari i Ri?

It prices with the wider centre: older stock at roughly 1,500 to 2,500 euros per square metre in 2026, and new build near the square at 3,000 to 3,500. The premium here is paid for footfall and short-let demand rather than for quiet or for family living.
What should I check before buying near Pazari i Ri?

Noise tolerance and the building's age. This is the busiest evening district in Tirana outside Blloku, which is the point for a short-let owner and a problem for a resident. Confirm the construction year and whether the block predates 2000, since older central stock carries a lasting structural discount.
21-dhjetori: How much does an apartment cost in 21 Dhjetori, Tirana?

New builds run about 1,800 to 2,200 euros per square metre in 2026. That is roughly half what Blloku commands, for a district that sits directly beside both Blloku and the centre, which is the whole argument for buying here rather than one street further in.
Is 21 Dhjetori a good area to invest in?

It works for rental income aimed at young professionals. The location is genuinely central and the entry price is mid-market, so the yield arithmetic is better than in Blloku. Buy it as a letting asset rather than as a home, and price the noise into what you are willing to pay.
What is the main problem with 21 Dhjetori?

It is built around the busiest junction in Tirana, and the traffic noise is constant rather than occasional. Floor level and which way the windows face change the experience of the same building substantially here, so view a specific apartment at rush hour before you decide anything.
bulevardi-i-ri: How much does property cost on Tirana's New Boulevard?

First-line units start around 2,700 euros per square metre in 2026. The second line runs about 1,900 and rose roughly 36 percent in a single year, the fastest increase of any Tirana district. That gap between the two lines is the clearest arbitrage currently visible in the city.
Is the New Boulevard a good investment?

It is the city's main transformation zone and its most speculative one. The masterplan covers about a fifth of Tirana and includes relocating the municipality and courts, plus a Qatari-funded square. The upside is real on a three to seven year horizon; the timing depends on state projects delivering.
What is the risk on the New Boulevard?

The price already assumes the plan is delivered. A 36 percent jump in one year on the second line means buyers are paying today for institutions and public works that have not yet moved. If the state timetable slips, and Albanian public projects have slipped before, that premium sits idle.
don-bosko: How much does an apartment cost in Don Bosko, Tirana?

New builds run about 1,500 to 2,000 euros per square metre in 2026, roughly a third of central Blloku prices. Rents sit about 100 to 300 euros a month below equivalent Blloku units, which is why the district reads better on yield than on prestige.
Is Don Bosko a good area to live in Tirana?

It suits families who want city life without central prices. The district has cafes, markets, a park and the GDQ school, and it has been gentrifying steadily rather than in a speculative burst. The main compromise is density: the building stock is packed tightly and green space is limited.

Yes, and at a measured pace. It is one of the districts our research flags as making the transition earlier than neighbours like Kombinat, which is part of why it now sits at 1,500 to 2,000 euros per square metre rather than at 1,000. The easy repricing here has largely happened.
ali-demi: How much does an apartment cost in Ali Demi, Tirana?

New builds run about 1,400 to 1,800 euros per square metre in 2026. That is one of the better price-to-centre ratios in Tirana: the district is genuinely close in, and it costs roughly half what comparable proximity commands on the other side of the city centre.
Is Ali Demi a good area to buy?

It is old Tirana in transition. The district holds Continental Hospital and the Bektashi World Centre, and it has been gentrifying without the speculative pricing seen on the New Boulevard. For a buyer who wants proximity at a mid-market price, it is one of the more defensible entries in the city.
What should I check before buying in Ali Demi?

The age and condition of the specific building. This is an older part of the city, so the stock spans decades and quality varies street by street. Confirm the construction year, and treat anything built before 2000 with the same caution the market applies after the 2019 earthquake.
fresku: How much does property cost in Fresku, Tirana?

Prices run about 1,400 to 1,500 euros per square metre in 2026, up from 1,100 to 1,200 in 2024. That is a rise of roughly 16 to 27 percent in a year, driven by the new road connecting the area to the Grand Ring rather than by any change in the housing itself.

One road. The new connection to the Grand Ring cut the district's isolation, and the market repriced accordingly, by 16 to 27 percent in a year. The Dajti Express cable car and Bunkart1 sit nearby, and the air on the eastern slope is measurably better than in the centre.
What is the risk of buying in Fresku?

The thesis depends on a single road. Fresku's repricing came almost entirely from improved access to the Grand Ring, so its value is tied to that one connection continuing to function and to further eastern infrastructure arriving. That is a narrower base than districts supported by jobs or year-round demand.
astir-unaza-e-re: How much does an apartment cost in Astir, Tirana?

New builds start around 1,400 euros per square metre in 2026, up from 1,200 to 1,300 in 2024. Government reference prices in this zone were raised by a record 76 percent in 2023, which pulled up both the tax base and seller expectations across the whole south-west.
Is Astir a good place to buy in Tirana?

It is the natural landing spot for young families priced out of the centre, and it is the largest new-build front in south-west Tirana. That scale is also the problem: our research flags oversupply here as the single biggest risk in the Tirana market, ahead of any other district.
What happens to Astir prices in a downturn?

This is where the discounts would appear first. Analysis cited in our research puts downside discounts at 10 to 15 percent in Astir specifically, because the volume of new supply gives buyers alternatives that other districts do not offer. The upside case rests on the railway and the completion of the ring road.
shkoze: How much does property cost in Shkozë, Tirana?

New complexes near the Grand Ring run at roughly 1,400 euros per square metre in 2026. Shkozë is priced as former periphery that has been absorbed into the city, which is what puts it well below the central districts while remaining inside Tirana proper.
Is Shkozë a good area to buy?

It suits a buyer prioritising price per square metre over amenity. The district was outer periphery until recently and its infrastructure is still catching up with the new construction along the Grand Ring. Check what is actually finished around a specific development rather than what the site plan promises.
What should I look at before buying in Shkozë?

Delivery of the surrounding infrastructure. At around 1,400 euros per square metre you are buying into an area still being built out, so the gap between the rendering and the street matters. Visit at the same time of day you would live there, and ask what is contracted versus what is proposed.
kashar: How much does property cost in Kashar?

The market runs about 1,000 to 1,400 euros per square metre in 2026, with newer phases starting around 1,400. Kashar sits on the western corridor between Tirana and Durrës, alongside the QTU shopping centre, Tirana Business Park and the area's logistics employment.

Its case rests on the Tirana-Durrës railway. A rail link turning the two cities into one commuter region would reprice the corridor, and Kashar sits directly on it. Against that, the corridor carries a large volume of new supply, and an apartment here can end up a dormitory beside a highway.

Diaspora buyers, including returning pensioners, alongside households working in the corridor's business parks and logistics. The mix matters: diaspora demand is real but episodic, and it does not produce the steady year-round tenant base that central Tirana districts have. Model your occupancy on local employment rather than on visits home.
kombinat: How much does an apartment cost in Kombinat, Tirana?

New builds run about 1,000 to 1,300 euros per square metre in 2026, with resale at roughly 700 to 1,000. One-bedroom rents start around 150 to 200 euros a month. That makes Kombinat the cheapest genuine city district in Tirana rather than a suburb at a distance.

Our research flags it as undervalued. Kombinat is a 1950s industrial town built around the textile works, six kilometres from the centre, with a real identity and early-stage gentrification rather than a completed one. The comparison we would draw is Don Bosko, which made the same transition earlier and now costs more.
How long is the Kombinat thesis?

Five years rather than two. The gentrification here is at an early stage, and the district's repricing depends on the same slow process that moved Don Bosko from cheap to mid-market. Buy it for the entry price and the identity, and do not expect the New Boulevard's pace of movement.
laprake: Is Laprakë a good area to invest in Tirana?

It is among the fastest-gentrifying districts in the city according to analysis cited in our research. Laprakë holds the trauma hospital, the American Hospital, the new regional bus station and the aerodrome, and it sits on the planned Tirana-Durrës-Rinas rail junction, which is the main driver behind its case.
How much does property cost in Laprakë?

There is no reliable district-level price series for Laprakë specifically. The market treats it as part of the Dritan Hoxha corridor rather than as a separate zone, so quoted figures generally reflect that corridor. Ask an agent for comparable transactions in the exact building rather than accepting a district average.
What is the main driver for Laprakë?

The rail junction. Laprakë sits on the planned Tirana-Durrës-Rinas connection, and its case depends on that infrastructure arriving. The hospitals and the regional bus station already give it real daily footfall, which is more than several other districts with a similar price can claim.
kamez: How much does property cost in Kamëz?

Phase-one bookings in the Ulliri zone run about 750 to 900 euros per square metre in 2026. That is the lowest entry price anywhere in the Tirana agglomeration, and the discount to central Tirana is a straightforward reflection of the risks attached rather than a market oversight.
Is Kamëz a good place to buy?

Only with the legal work done first and the risks priced in. Kamëz carries the highest combination of title uncertainty, weak transport links and reputational discount in the agglomeration. At 750 to 900 euros per square metre the price acknowledges that; the mistake is treating it as a bargain rather than as compensation.
What are the risks in Kamëz?

Title, transport and reputation, in that order. Ownership documentation in the wider Kamëz area is the least reliable near Tirana, connections to the city are limited, and resale depends on a buyer pool that shares your risk tolerance. Engage a lawyer before any deposit moves, without exception.
paskuqan: How much does property cost in Paskuqan?

Existing stock runs about 600 to 1,100 euros per square metre in 2026, and new build reaches roughly 1,200, up around 14 percent year on year from 850 to 900 in 2023. That makes Paskuqan the cheapest entry into greater Tirana after Kamëz.
Is Paskuqan a safe place to buy property?

It requires more legal care than anywhere else on this list. Paskuqan was the largest informal construction zone of the 1990s, and the legalisation process through the state cadastre has been slow. Confirm the legalisation status of the specific unit before paying anything, not the status of the area in general.
Why is Paskuqan new build approaching Astir prices?

Because sellers have followed the wider market rather than the fundamentals. New build at about 1,200 euros per square metre puts Paskuqan close to Astir, and our research flags that convergence as unjustified: the title risk is materially higher and the social and transport infrastructure is thinner.
farke-lunder: How much does a villa cost in Farkë and Lundër?

This is the most expensive reference zone in Albania, at 257,000 lek per square metre around Lake Farka, roughly 2,620 euros. Gated developments price accordingly: Rolling Hills Lake has listed at about 950,000 euros and a three-bedroom at Piccadilly at around 690,000.
Who buys in Farkë and Lundër?

Expatriate management and Albanian high earners, buying detached houses rather than apartments. The area south of the city around the TEG centre holds the country's main gated communities, including Long Hill, Rolling Hills and Farka Lake Shore, and the product is scarce enough that supply rarely meets demand.
Are Albanian villas a good investment?

For capital rather than income. Villas in Farkë, Lundër and Lalzi Bay sit in a genuinely thin segment with demand from the diaspora and from European buyers with specific requirements, which is a more durable pool than speculative apartment demand. The trade-off is liquidity: fewer buyers means a longer sale.
